title: Reserve hot write surfaces across the full task lifecycle
description: Prevent overlapping tasks from overtaking each other once a write surface becomes hot. Extend coordination so declared and observed write surfaces reserve a conflict cluster from start through running, finalize, merge repair, blocked conflict, retry, stop, or terminal integration.

userStories.title: Reserve observed conflict clusters while work is active
userStories.description: Use declared and observed write surfaces to hold a conflict cluster while a task is pending, running, ready to finalize, finalizing, or merge repairing.
acceptanceCriteria: A later task with overlapping declared or observed surfaces remains pending while an earlier owner is non-terminal.
The queue summary explains the owner task and conflict surface that caused the block.
Non-overlapping tasks in the same repo can still run up to the configured concurrency limit.

userStories.title: Release reservations only on explicit terminal states
userStories.description: Release hot-surface ownership only when the owner task integrates, is archived/stopped as terminal, or is explicitly demoted by retry policy.
acceptanceCriteria: Completed integrated tasks release their conflict cluster.
Failed or blocked-conflict tasks keep the cluster reserved until retry, stop, or explicit recovery changes state.
Tests cover running, ready_to_finalize, blocked_conflict, failed, stopped, and completed integrated transitions.

userStories.title: Expose cluster state for operators
userStories.description: Make hot-surface reservations visible in queue/status output so operators can see why a task is not starting.
acceptanceCriteria: Queue compact JSON includes coordination owner, phase, lane, and reason for hot-surface waits.
Human queue output keeps the message short and actionable.
npm test passes with scheduler and queue regression coverage.
